# Data governance and safety

## Data used in this submission
**100% synthetic.** Generated by `backend/app/seed.py` with planted effects (distance, gender) so that the analytics can be
tested. No real patient, no scraped data, no third-party dataset. Names, phones and villages are fictitious
(all numbers start +91 90000, a placeholder block). The one external fact used in the Impact tab is a published
study cited with its link.

## If real data is used (pilot)
| Principle | How CuraLoop supports it |
|---|---|
| Purpose limitation | Used only for screening follow-up; no secondary use, no advertising |
| Data minimisation | Stores contact, village, screening result and journey events; no diagnosis text, no photos |
| Consent | Per-patient consent flag. A patient replying STOP is opted out on the spot, further messages are blocked and the change is audited; staff can record consent again |
| Access control | Three roles, enforced server-side; in secure mode identity comes from a signed token, not a header |
| Accountability | Append-only audit log of every state change, message approval and rule edit |
| Human oversight | Outbound messages go through an approval queue in phase 1 |
| Sharing | Manager-only de-identified export (pseudonym, age band, sex, state; no name, phone, ABHA id or village), and every export is logged |
| Residency | Self-hostable; the district can run it on its own infrastructure |

The design is aligned with the principles of India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (consent,
purpose limitation, minimisation, security safeguards, breach handling). **This is not a legal compliance
claim**; a legal review and a data-processing agreement are prerequisites for any live data.

## Security controls in the code
Signed expiring tokens (HMAC-SHA256), PBKDF2 password hashing, login rate limit, security headers, no-store caching for API
responses, signed WhatsApp webhooks (`X-Hub-Signature-256`), demo tools disabled in secure mode, secrets only from environment.

## Known limits
No retention or deletion scheduler yet, no SSO, no field-level encryption at rest (rely on database/volume encryption), no external pen-test yet, in-memory rate limiter (single instance).
